home.kicker: Quantum-resistant encryption · Shareware · Windows, macOS, Linux
home.title: Smaller archives than 7-Zip, RAR and ZIP.
home.lead: NikPak recognises photos, music and office documents by their content and compresses each file with the codec that suits it best. Every encrypted archive is quantum-resistant: 256-bit symmetric encryption only, with no RSA or elliptic curves for a quantum computer to break.
home.free_note: Free for personal use · unNik, the archive browser, is free for everyone

stats.l: up to this much smaller than ZIP
quantum-resistant encryption: no RSA, no elliptic curves

home.why_sub: One small program, designed around four ideas: compress better, go faster, protect with modern cryptography, run unchanged everywhere.

cards.d: Only 256-bit symmetric cryptography. There is no RSA, elliptic-curve or Diffie-Hellman code for a quantum computer to break.
WAV, AIFF, ProTracker MOD and BMP files are recognised by their content, not their name. Each one is tried with several lossless filters and the smallest result wins.
The Deflate streams inside docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, epub, pdf, zip and gz files are unpacked, compressed far better and rebuilt bit for bit when you extract.
At -m5 NikPak picks LZMA2 or PPMd for each block and sorts files by type. It made the smallest archive of all four tools on every test set.
At the fast level -m2, 190 MB of source code is archived in 1.7 s on one core, 56 times faster than 7-Zip's default level.
Argon2id with 64 MiB of memory and XChaCha20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption. File names, sizes and dates are always hidden, and tampering is always detected.

features.title: Features
features.sub: What is inside NikPak and the .nik format, explained plainly.
features.media_p1: NikPak looks at what a file contains, not at its extension. WAV and AIFF audio, ProTracker MOD music and BMP images are recognised and sent through filters made for them.
features.media_p2: Every media file goes through a trial: NAC, Shuffle, Shuffle+Delta and MED are tried and the smallest result is kept. When no filter helps, the file is compressed normally, so a filter never makes an archive bigger.
media_list: NAC, NikPak's lossless audio codec: linear prediction and stereo decorrelation, on par with FLAC -8.
Self-verification: every NAC block is decoded again during compression and compared with the original.
Shuffle and Shuffle+Delta for samples and pixels, and a dedicated path for ProTracker MOD files.
Results against RAR 7 -m5: BMP photographs 38.8 % smaller, stereo music 14.6 %, MOD files 13.3 %.
features.office_p: docx, xlsx, pptx, odt, ods, epub, jar, zip, pdf and gz files hide their content in Deflate streams that ordinary compressors cannot shrink any more. At levels -m4 and -m5 NikPak decodes these streams, compresses the plain data far better and rebuilds the original file bit for bit when you extract. On 60 office files the archive is 31.7 % smaller than with 7-Zip -mx9.
features.engine_p: Levels -m1 to -m4 use a multi-threaded, solid Zstandard stream, with a 128 MiB window and long-distance matching at -m4. The maximum level -m5, the default, builds a multi-engine body: LZMA2 for binary data and PPMd for text, chosen by trial, with files sorted by type.
levels: Fast: the choice when speed matters more than size
High: adds Deflate recompression for office files, PDF and gzip
Maximum, the default: LZMA2 and PPMd chosen by trial
features.crypto_p: Encrypted archives use Argon2id to turn the password into a key. It needs 64 MiB of memory for every guess, which makes password guessing on graphics cards expensive. The data is then encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 in authenticated chunks of 64 KiB.
crypto_list: File names, sizes, dates and permissions are always encrypted.
Reordering, truncation and header changes are detected cryptographically.
No password given? NikPak generates a strong one: 24 characters, about 139 bits.
There is no back door: a lost password cannot be recovered by anyone.
features.quantum_p1: Quantum computers threaten public-key cryptography: Shor's algorithm breaks RSA and elliptic curves. NikPak uses none of them. Its encryption is 256-bit symmetric only, which keeps about 128 bits of security even against Grover's algorithm.
features.quantum_p2: Archives captured today cannot simply be decrypted later by a quantum computer ("harvest now, decrypt later"). The strength of your password still matters most, and Argon2id makes guessing it expensive.
safety_list: Extraction never writes outside the destination folder (zip-slip protection).
Symbolic links are refused and setuid bits are removed.
Every decoder has strict limits: a malicious archive cannot exhaust memory.
Archives are written atomically: a failed run never leaves a half-written file.
CRC32 of every file, an end marker with the entry count, and a program written in memory-safe Rust.
features.apps_p: NikPak creates archives from a single drop window; unNik opens, browses and extracts them. Both share the language, the sounds and the settings, and one button switches from one to the other.
limits_list: Recovery records that can repair a damaged archive
Adding or replacing files inside an existing archive
Decades of field testing and millions of existing .rar files
roadmap_list: Recovery records: Reed-Solomon parity to repair damaged archives.
Multi-volume archives and updates: splitting large archives, adding and replacing files.
Sharing with public keys: a hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM, safe if either one holds.
More media filters: floating-point audio, XM/S3M/IT trackers, PNG recompression, TGA and TIFF.
ZIP and RAR in unNik: unpack the common formats in unNik, so that NikPak can be the only archiver you need. (The file-manager menu shipped in 1.5.5.)
A faster maximum level: multi-threaded LZMA2 and PPMd, deduplication, a filter for executables.
An external security review of the cryptography and the extractor.
features.skins_p: 55 skins for NikPak and unNik: the 41 of Nikkomander plus 14 painted ones of our own. The choice is saved and shared by both programs, and you can import your own .skin.json skins.

bench.title: Benchmarks
bench.sub: NikPak, RAR 7.00, 7-Zip 23.01 and Info-ZIP 3.0, run one after another on the same machine and the same files.
method_list: Linux x86-64 virtual machine (Intel Xeon, 2.8 GHz). Every tool pinned to one CPU core and run single-threaded.
Maximum levels: nikpak -m5, RAR -m5 -s, 7-Zip -mx9, ZIP -9. Fast levels: nikpak -m2, RAR -m3 -s, 7-Zip -mx5, ZIP -6.
All 92 archives were extracted again and compared with the originals: all were identical.

Public test material: scikit-image photographs, the libxmp MOD collection, LibreOffice gallery sounds, music rendered with TiMidity++, Project Gutenberg books, office files, the Python standard library and C headers.
bench.chart_t: Archive size at the maximum level
bench.chart_sub: Percentage of the original size, lower is better.
bench.max_t: Maximum level: archive size in bytes
bench.max_note: The smallest archive in each row is highlighted.
bench.fast_t: Fast levels: size and creation time
bench.fast_note: Archive size as a percentage of the original, and creation time on one core. The smallest archive in each row is highlighted.
bench.gen_note: 190 MB, 11,473 files: Python libraries, C headers and documentation.
reading_list: NikPak -m5 is the smallest on every set: 2.4 to 31.7 % smaller than 7-Zip -mx9, 10.8 to 38.4 % smaller than RAR 7 -m5 and 19.9 to 60.4 % smaller than ZIP -9.
Recorded audio: on the 24-bit music 7-Zip saves 12 % and NikPak 37 %, because the NAC codec predicts what general compressors can only match.
Office files, 31.7 % smaller than 7-Zip, thanks to Deflate recompression. The price at -m5 is time: 81 s against 26 s.
Text, 15.9 % smaller in half the time: PPMd wins on prose. It decodes as slowly as it encodes, so extraction takes 2.7 s instead of 0.2 s.
Fast level -m2: 1.7 s for the general set, against 93.7 s for 7-Zip -mx5, 48.2 s for RAR and 7.3 s for ZIP. It is not the smallest on text and source code, which is why -m5 is the default.
Extraction: 0.9 s (-m2) or 5.6 s (-m5) for the general set, against 6.0 s for 7-Zip, 6.7 s for RAR and 6.9 s for ZIP.
The cost: -m5 is single-threaded and slower than 7-Zip on large office and source-code sets. A faster maximum level is on the roadmap.
bench.source_note: Figures from the NikPak technical guide (section 11.7, NikPak 1.2.0). Measure on your own files: nikpak mt shows what each media filter achieves without writing anything.

guide.title: User guide
guide.sub: Install NikPak, compress with a drop, browse archives with unNik, register, and drive everything from the command line.
guide.install_p1: Run the setup. By default it installs for the current user only, without administrator rights, into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\NikPak; its first page also offers to install for all users. It installs NikPak and unNik, adds them to the Start menu, puts NikPak on the desktop and makes unNik the program for .nik files. On request it adds the folder to the PATH for the command line.
guide.install_p2: Updates install over the previous version and keep your licence.
win_steps: Start NikPak. Drop files or folders on the window, or click the circle and choose Choose files or Choose a folder.

They are compressed with the best compression (-m5) into one archive named after the file, the folder, or the folder they came from. An existing archive is never overwritten: report.nik becomes report (2).nik.
The ring shows the percentage, the phase (analysing, compressing, finishing), the amount processed and the time. Cancel or Esc stops at once and removes the unfinished archive.
When the ring turns green: Show in folder, Open in unNik, or Compress more.
win_more: Save to: the destination folder at the bottom. It is remembered; the first time it is the Desktop. The folder button next to it opens it.
Switch to unNik: the round button left of the i button closes NikPak and opens unNik, with the new archive if you just made one.
Language: the button at the bottom left. NikPak and unNik restart in the chosen language and share it.
Sounds: the speaker button in the title bar switches the sound effects on and off.

Skins: the palette button in the title bar opens the skins menu beside the window (click a skin to try it, Apply Skin to keep it, Cancel to go back); the sun / moon button switches between dark and bright. The choice is remembered and shared with unNik. All the skins.
Status and About: the top left shows EVALUATION COPY · REGISTER or the licence holder; the i button shows the version and the licence.
guide.admin_note: Running as administrator? Windows does not allow dragging files from Explorer onto a program that runs as administrator. NikPak restarts itself once as a normal user; if that is not possible, choose the files with the buttons instead.
guide.unnik_p: Double-click a .nik file, drop it on the unNik window or pick one of the recent archives. Encrypted archives ask for their password first. The window grows into a browser with the folder tree, the files and the details of the selected file.
unnik_list: Navigate with the folder tree, the breadcrumbs, Back, Forward and Up, and double-clicks. Search finds files by name in the whole archive.
Select with a click, Ctrl+click, Shift+click or the check boxes. Click a column title to sort. A right-click opens a menu with every action.
Extract all or the selection: choose the destination, keep the folders or not, and what to do when a file exists: replace it, keep both or skip it.
View text with line numbers and search, or binary files in hexadecimal. Open starts a file with its own program.
Delete removes files from the archive after a confirmation; the archive is written again safely. Test checks every file.
keys: Extract the selection (everything when nothing is selected)
reg_steps: Buy a licence. You receive a key that starts with NPK1- by e-mail.
In NikPak, click EVALUATION COPY · REGISTER at the top left, or Register in the reminder.
Enter the name and the e-mail address exactly as on your licence, and paste the key. Case, extra spaces and the look-alike characters O/0 and I/L/1 do not matter.
guide.reg_p: Once registered, NikPak never asks again on that computer. A company can instead put a nikpak.key file next to nikpak.exe, which registers every user of that PC. From the command line:
guide.cli_p: NikPak follows the syntax RAR users know: nikpak <command> [options] <archive> [files...]. Options may come before or after the archive name; -- ends the options.
commands: a
Create an archive. .nik is added when the name has no extension. Folders are always included with their contents.
x
Extract with full paths: everything, or only the names, folders and wildcards given.
e
Extract without paths: every file goes straight into the destination folder.
l
List the contents: attributes, size, date, name and totals.
v
Verbose list: adds the CRC32 of every file.
lb
Bare list: one name per line, for scripts and front-ends.
t
Test: decompress everything and check every CRC32 and, when encrypted, the authentication.
p
Print files to the standard output.
d
Delete files or folders from an archive. Encrypted archives keep their password.
mt
Media test: shows the size each media filter achieves. Writes nothing.
register
Register a licence: nikpak register "Name" e-mail key. Also license and unregister.
options: Encrypt or decrypt and ask for the password. An empty entry generates a random password.
Password on the command line (visible to other users of the machine).
Same as -p; file names are always encrypted in NikPak.
Recurse into folders (always on; accepted for compatibility).
Compression level: store, fastest, fast, good, high, maximum (default).
Number of threads, 1 to 256 (default: all cores).
All content filters off / media filters always on. Default: automatic trial per file.
Store only the file name, without its path.
Do not store the name of the base folder.
Rename extracted files that already exist: name (1).ext.
Destination folder for x and e.
Read file names from a text file, one per line.
guide.pwd_p: When an archive is created with -p, NikPak takes the password from, in this order:
pwd_list: -p<password> or -P <password> on the command line (at least 8 characters);
the environment variable NIKPAK_PASSWORD, which keeps it out of the process list;
an interactive prompt, asked twice; an empty entry generates a random password;
without a terminal, a password piped on the standard input, else a generated one.
guide.pwd_note: A generated password has 24 characters from 56 unambiguous symbols, about 139 bits. It is shown once. There is no recovery: an archive whose password is lost cannot be opened by anyone.
exits: Some files were skipped (unreadable, unsafe path, symbolic link)
Cannot create or read a file
No file matched the names or wildcards
Bad password, or a tampered encrypted archive
guide.tc_p: Because NikPak accepts RAR's command syntax, a program that can drive an external rar.exe can drive nikpak.exe. In Total Commander, register the extension nik as an additional packer and point the packer and unpacker commands to nikpak.exe. Use -o+ or -y for unattended extraction. Options that RAR front-ends often send (-s, -ma5, -md64m, -ibck, -rr and similar) are accepted and ignored.
guide.tc_note: Folders with spaces on Windows: a quoted path that ends with a backslash, such as "C:\My Folder\", is misread by Windows. Use -d "C:\My Folder" instead.
guide.more_p: The technical guide describes the .nik format, the NAC codec, the encryption design and the complete benchmarks. Questions? Write to us.
guide.install_unix: macOS and Linux: unpack the archive and run ./install.sh. It copies nikpak and unNik to ~/.local/bin (Linux) or /usr/local/bin (macOS) and adds the right-click menu of the file manager (Dolphin, Nemo, Nautilus; Quick Actions in the Finder). Then start the window with nikpak.
guide.skins_p: NikPak and unNik share 55 skins. The menu opens beside the program, so you can see the whole interface in the skin you are trying.
skins_steps: Click the palette button in the title bar. The window widens and the skins box appears on the right, outside the program.
Click a skin: the whole window takes its colours and its background at once.
Drag the box by its title bar if you want it elsewhere, or to compare it with the interface behind.
Click Apply Skin to keep it, or Cancel (Esc, or the ×) to go back to the skin you had.
guide.skins_note: The choice is saved and shared by NikPak and unNik. The painted skins (Moon, Pattaya Neons, Amiga, Chess…) are drawn by the program itself; Import a skin… at the bottom of the box adds a Nikkomander .skin.json.
guide.menu_p: A “NikPak” submenu in the file manager’s right-click menu, like WinRAR’s, is installed by the Windows setup (a checked-by-default option) and by nikpak --install-menu on Linux; macOS gets Finder Quick Actions.
menu_list: On files and folders: Add to archive… (asks for the name and the folder, then compresses in the NikPak window) and Add to archive here (the archive goes next to the items, named like a drop on the window).
On .nik archives: Open with unNik, Extract files…, Extract here and Extract to its own folder.
Several items go into one archive; several selected archives are extracted one after the other in one window.
The commands run through unNik.exe, so no console window flashes; the labels follow the language of NikPak. Windows 10 shows the submenu directly, Windows 11 under Show more options (Shift+F10).
The menu uses nikpak --add and --add-here, and unNik --extract, --extract-here and --extract-to.
guide.menu_note: A second setup, unnik-<version>-setup.exe, installs unNik alone — the free archive browser — for people who only receive .nik archives.

skins.title: 55 skins, one click
skins.sub: NikPak and unNik wear the same skins as Nikkomander, from Nikkoid Blue to Pizza, Matrix and 8-Bit Game. Pick one and both programs keep it.
how_list: Skins button: the palette button in the title bar opens the skins menu. The box opens beside the window, so the whole interface stays visible: click a skin to try it on the window.
Apply or cancel: the box can be dragged anywhere by its title bar. Apply Skin keeps the skin for NikPak and unNik; Cancel (or Esc) goes back to the one you had.
Sun and moon: the button next to it switches between Nikkoid Blue (dark) and Nikkoid Bright in one click, like in Nikkomander.
Remembered: the chosen skin is saved and used at the next start. NikPak and unNik share it: change it in one, the other follows within seconds.

Painted and flat: 41 skins from Nikkomander's CSS gradients - stripes, stars, bricks - and 14 new ones whose artwork NikPak draws itself: a storm, mountains at dusk, a neon street, old computers, a chessboard. They stay sharp at any window size. Since 1.6.2 the painted artwork steps behind the interface - softened and faded behind the title, the drop ring and the status text - so it never competes with the window.
skins.gallery_sub: NikPak in every skin. Click a picture to see it full size.
skins.unnik_p: The archive browser follows the same skin: folders, file icons, selection and dialogs take the skin's colours.
skins.custom_p: A skin is a small .skin.json file: a name and a list of colours, in the same format as Nikkomander. Click Import a skin… at the bottom of the skins menu: the file is copied to the skins folder next to the settings, and the × on its tile removes it again.
skins.limits: NikPak keeps its own fonts in every skin; the fonts and a few decorative borders of Nikkomander's skins are not used.
skins.new_p: Moon, America, Pattaya Neons, Burgers Tokyo, Sushi, Amiga Computer, MSX Computer, Colecovision, ZX Spectrum, Cat Life, Dog Life, Mario Bros, Counter Strike and Chess: artwork drawn by NikPak itself, not a gradient, so it stays sharp at any window size.
